properties.trigger: any competition in tennis; a tennis match, set score, draw, seed, ranking, doubles pair, team tie or rubber, box league, ladder, retirement or walkover; a tennis stat key or stage not yet in this world; the first racket or individual sport added to this world (pickleball, padel, badminton, table tennis, squash read the chunk Other racket sports)
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, venue, stat_line

data.short_description: Tennis at every level: tour and major tournaments, national-team ties, college dual matches, club leagues, box leagues, ladders and social play. The pattern pack for individual and racket sports: a person (or a doubles pair, a team with team_type pair) is a side; a tournament is a competition whose editions are seasons; a team tie is a parent event with rubbers as children; sets won is the score number and the full line is in score_display; rankings are stored snapshots; retirements and walkovers carry no reason. Pickleball, padel, badminton, table tennis and squash copy this pattern (see Other racket sports).

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport: tennis. Code tennis. This is the first individual (racket) sport pack and sets the pattern that pickleball, padel, badminton, table tennis and squash copy (see the chunk Other racket sports).

What a match is: one match between two sides. A side is a person (singles) or a doubles pair (a team with team_type pair; see Doubles pairs). In team competitions (national-team ties, college dual matches, club and association league team matches) the team match is called a tie and is a parent event; each singles or doubles match inside it is a rubber, a child event PART_OF the tie, and the sides of the rubber are still people or pairs.

Parts of a match: points make games, games make sets, sets make the match. A set is won at 6 games with a two-game lead, or by a tiebreak at 6-6 (first to 7 points, two clear). Many formats end a deciding set with a match tiebreak (first to 10, two clear) instead of a full set. Variants: pro set (first to 8 games, tiebreak at 8-8), short sets (first to 4), timed play, single set. The format is match_format on the competition (the default) or on the event (an override); values are in Stages and rounds.

The single score number. home_score and away_score are SETS WON in any best-of-sets format (2-1, 3-0). In pro-set, single-set and timed formats they are GAMES WON (8-6). In a team tie the parent event's score is RUBBERS WON (3-2). The AI must read match_format before interpreting the number. score_display always carries the full line as tennis writes it: games per set separated by spaces, loser's tiebreak points in brackets after the tiebreak set, a match tiebreak written as a 1-0 set with the points in brackets, and the stoppage marker if the match did not finish:
  6-4 3-6 7-6(5)
  6-2 6-3
  4-6 6-3 [10-7]  (match tiebreak in place of a third set; write 1-0(7) only if the owner prefers)
  8-6  (pro set)
  6-4 3-6 2-5 ret.  (retirement at 2-5 in the third)
  w/o  (walkover; no score)
  6-3 2-1 def.  (default)
The first-named side's games come first in every set. In a tie the parent event's score_display is "3-2". The set-by-set line may also go in the event's periods array when the owner wants it queryable: one element per set with number, home and away games, and kind (set, tiebreak_set, match_tiebreak, with the tiebreak points in a points key); score_display stays the human line. margin_type is sets (margin the difference in sets won) in best-of-sets formats and games (margin the games difference) in pro-set, single-set and timed formats; both are blank for a walkover, which has no score.

Draws and ties: tennis has no draws. result is home_win or away_win when completed, pending before, no_result only for an abandoned match that will not be resumed (rare: a rain-stopped match is resumed later from the same score, and the event keeps its date_* of the first day with end_date the finishing day). An unfinished rubber in a tie that was not needed is status cancelled with result no_result and a lore note "not played, tie decided".

Sides and home. Most tennis is at a neutral site: neutral_site true, the first-named side COMPETED_IN side neutral_first (its score is home_score), the other neutral_second. In a draw the player printed higher in the draw is first-named. In a club ladder the challenger is first-named. In a team tie the host team is home and its players' rubbers use side home/away.

Default competition shape: a tournament is a competition with format knockout (group_knockout for a round-robin-then-knockout finals event) and each edition is a season; the tour year is a competition with format league and scoring_system ranking_points; a club league or association team league is format league or league_playoffs with scoring_system win_loss or rubbers; a box league is format round_robin; a ladder is format ladder. Full mapping in Tournaments and tours.

Edges: a singles player COMPETED_IN the match (side, result); no PLAYED_IN edge is used in singles because the COMPETED_IN edge is the appearance. A pair COMPETED_IN the match and each partner PLAYED_IN it with for_team the pair's slug. In a tie the two teams COMPETED_IN the tie, each rubber's sides COMPETED_IN the rubber, and each squad member PLAYED_IN the tie with for_team their team and position the lineup slot. A person or pair enters a tournament edition, box or ladder with COMPETES_IN the season (seed, group, entry, status, outcome, final_rank). A tournament season is PART_OF the tour season it belongs to (see Tournaments and tours).

Units: court dimensions and ball specs are not tracked. Surface is venue.surface: hard, clay, grass, carpet, artificial_clay, artificial_grass, other. indoor true for indoor courts. A multi-court venue names the court on HELD_AT field ("Court 3", "Centre Court" is fine as a generic phrase).

Health and reasons: retirements, walkovers, defaults and withdrawals are recorded as sporting facts only. The reason is never stored, not even "illness", not even in lore. Say so once in one line if the owner volunteers it; never argue.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Tennis has no fixed positions. PLAYS_FOR.position is used only in these cases:

Doubles pair roster (person PLAYS_FOR a team with team_type pair):
  deuce_side   returns on the deuce (right) court
  ad_side      returns on the advantage (left) court
  unknown      when the owner has not said

Team tie squads (person PLAYS_FOR a national, school, club or recreational team): position is the lineup slot the player usually fills, and PLAYED_IN.position on the tie is the slot on the day:
  S1 S2 S3 S4 S5 S6   singles lineup order, 1 is the top player
  D1 D2 D3            doubles lineup order
  singles             a singles-only squad member when the order is not kept
  doubles             a doubles-only squad member
  reserve             travelling or named but not in the lineup

Player style descriptors are NOT positions. person.handedness takes: right, left, both. Backhand and play style go in the person's description or a tag (one_handed_backhand, two_handed_backhand, serve_and_volley, baseliner, all_court), never in position. PLAYS_FOR.role uses the base enum: captain for a tie team's playing captain, starter and reserve for a dual-match lineup, bench is not used.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage on a match event, by competition shape.

Tournament (knockout draw), main draw rounds by draw size. Use the code; round carries the human label when it helps ("R2", "Round of 32"):
  round_of_128   R128 (first round of a 128 draw)
  round_of_64    R64
  round_of_32    R32
  round_of_16    R16
  quarterfinal   QF
  semifinal      SF
  final          F
  third_place    bronze or third-place match where played
Qualifying rounds: stage qualifying with round "Q1", "Q2", "Q3" (final qualifying round). Pre-qualifying: stage pre_qualifying.
Round-robin finals event (group_knockout): stage group_stage with round "RR1".."RR3", then semifinal and final. The group letter or name is COMPETES_IN.group.
Consolation, back-draw or feed-in draws (common in junior and club events): stage consolation with round as the draw prints it ("Consolation QF").
Doubles and mixed are separate seasons of separate competitions or separate seasons of the same tournament competition (see Tournaments and tours); their rounds use the same codes.

Team ties and dual matches:
  The tie itself (parent event): stage from the team competition's calendar: group_stage, qualifying, playoff, round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, final, regular_season (league team matches), promotion_playoff, relegation_playoff.
  Each rubber (child event PART_OF the tie): stage rubber. round is the rubber label as the competition writes it: "Rubber 1", "Singles 1", "Doubles 2", "S3", "D1". Day of a multi-day tie goes on date_*; the tie carries end_date.

Club, league and casual:
  regular_season   league or box-league match
  box              a box-league match when the owner prefers it to regular_season (pick one per competition)
  ladder           a ladder challenge; round "Challenge" plus the ladder positions if the owner says them ("7 v 5")
  playoff          club league playoff
  final            club championship final
  exhibition       exhibition, charity, pro-am
  friendly         a hit with a score the owner wants kept
  practice is NOT a stage: a practice set goes on an event with event_type practice and no result.

Season.stage values (where the season is right now): entries_open, qualifying, main_draw, completed (tournaments); preseason, regular_season, playoffs, offseason (leagues and team competitions); cycle (box leagues: one cycle per season); open (ladders: always open while the season runs).

match_format values (competition default, event override; pick the closest and put anything odd in House rules):
  best_of_5                     five sets, full deciding set (tiebreak rules per the competition's House rules)
  best_of_5_match_tiebreak      five sets, 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 in the fifth
  best_of_3                     three sets, full third set
  best_of_3_match_tiebreak      two sets then a 10-point match tiebreak in place of a third set
  best_of_3_short_sets          sets to 4, used in some junior, senior and fast formats
  pro_set_8                     first to 8 games, tiebreak at 8-8; score number is games
  pro_set_10                    first to 10 games
  single_set                    one set; score number is games
  single_set_no_ad              one set, no-ad scoring
  timed                         play to a clock; score number is games
  tiebreak_only                 one 10-point (or 7-point) tiebreak; score number is 1-0, points in score_display
No-ad scoring, let-serve rules and tiebreak-at-12-12 variants are House rules, not formats.

decided_by values:
  regulation      finished normally (also for a match tiebreak that is part of the format)
  retired         one side stopped mid-match; opponent wins; score at stoppage in score_display with "ret."; no reason recorded
  walkover        one side did not start; opponent advances; status forfeited, result to the opponent, score_display "w/o", no reason recorded
  default         a side was defaulted by the officials; status forfeited or completed per the owner, score_display with "def."; no reason recorded
  decided_tie     a tie was decided before all rubbers were played, and dead rubbers were shortened or not played
  shortened       a rubber played under a shortened format by agreement (dead rubber, weather)
  coin_toss       used by some club events when a match cannot be played; say so in House rules

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, numbers only, null for not recorded. A rate marked DERIVED is never stored; the AI computes it from the stored keys when asked and says how many matches the components cover. A rate marked STORED-IF-GIVEN is stored only when the owner or a box score gives it and the components are unknown; set the components to null.

PLAYER MATCH LINE (scope match, STAT_OF the person, RECORDED_IN the match; in doubles, one line per partner only when the box score splits them, otherwise one line STAT_OF the pair). for_team: blank in singles, the pair slug in doubles, the team slug for a rubber in a tie. completeness: full when every key below that the owner tracks was recorded, partial when some are null, unknown for a typed-in line; season sums skip nulls. Per-set splits from a broadcast box score are separate lines with scope segment and segment "Set 3", RECORDED_IN the match, using the same keys; the match line is still the one season lines sum.

Serve
  aces                       serves the returner did not touch, point won
  double_faults              two faults in a row, point lost
  first_serves_in            first serves that landed in
  serve_points_played        total points on this player's serve (equals first serves attempted)
  first_serve_points_played  points where the first serve was in (equals first_serves_in; stored separately only on imported box scores)
  first_serve_points_won     points won when the first serve was in
  second_serve_points_played points played on a second serve (serve_points_played - first_serves_in)
  second_serve_points_won    points won on a second serve (double faults count as lost)
  service_games_played       games this player served
  service_games_won          service games held
  break_points_faced         break points the opponent had on this player's serve
  break_points_saved         of those, saved
  fastest_serve_kph          fastest serve in km/h (broadcast stat)
  average_first_serve_kph    average first-serve speed in km/h
  average_second_serve_kph   average second-serve speed in km/h
  first_serve_pct            DERIVED: first_serves_in / serve_points_played. STORED-IF-GIVEN as a percentage 0-100.
  first_serve_win_pct        DERIVED: first_serve_points_won / first_serves_in
  second_serve_win_pct       DERIVED: second_serve_points_won / second_serve_points_played
  hold_pct                   DERIVED: service_games_won / service_games_played
  break_points_saved_pct     DERIVED: break_points_saved / break_points_faced

Return
  return_points_played       points on the opponent's serve
  return_points_won          of those, won
  first_serve_return_points_won   return points won against a first serve
  second_serve_return_points_won  return points won against a second serve
  return_games_played        games the opponent served
  break_points_won           break points converted (breaks of serve)
  break_points_played        break-point opportunities (also called break points had)
  return_win_pct             DERIVED: return_points_won / return_points_played
  break_pct                  DERIVED: break_points_won / break_points_played

Rally and shot
  winners                    clean winners, all shots
  unforced_errors            unforced errors, all shots
  forced_errors              errors forced by the opponent (broadcast stat, often absent)
  forehand_winners           winners by shot type when the box score splits them
  backhand_winners
  forehand_unforced_errors
  backhand_unforced_errors
  net_points_played          approaches to the net
  net_points_won
  volley_winners
  overhead_winners
  drop_shot_winners
  net_pct                    DERIVED: net_points_won / net_points_played

Totals and match
  total_points_played
  total_points_won           points won in the match
  games_won                  games won (sum over sets)
  games_lost
  sets_won
  sets_lost
  tiebreaks_played
  tiebreaks_won
  longest_rally_shots        longest rally in shots (broadcast stat)
  distance_covered_m         metres run (tracking stat), per match
  match_duration_min         minutes from first point to last; a match fact, stored on the winner's AND loser's line if the owner wants it on lines, otherwise in lore on the event
  points_win_pct             DERIVED: total_points_won / total_points_played
  dominance_ratio            DERIVED: return_win_pct / (1 - (serve points won / serve points played)); serve points won = first_serve_points_won + second_serve_points_won

Challenges and conduct (optional)
  challenges_made            electronic review challenges used
  challenges_won
  code_violations            warnings and point penalties as a count; the conduct code itself never goes in stats
  time_violations

PLAYER SEASON AND CAREER LINES (scope season RECORDED_IN the tour season or the club season; scope career, no RECORDED_IN). Sums of the match keys above where the owner tracks match lines, plus:
  matches_played             completed matches (walkovers received are not matches played; walkovers given are not either)
  matches_won
  matches_lost
  walkovers_received         advanced without playing
  walkovers_given            did not start; no reason ever attached
  retirements                matches this player retired from; a count only, never joined to a reason
  defaults                   matches lost by default
  titles                     tournament wins (season or career)
  finals                     finals reached, including those won
  semifinals                 semifinals reached, including those won
  ranking                    STORED snapshot: ranking position as of as_of (tour or national ranking; the competition's House rules say which)
  ranking_points             STORED snapshot: points behind that ranking
  ranking_high               career line: best ranking reached
  rating                     STORED snapshot: a dynamic rating system's rating as of as_of (club and pickleball systems); which system is in House rules
  ladder_position            STORED snapshot: position on a club ladder as of as_of
  ladder_challenges_won
  ladder_challenges_lost
  prize_money                STORED, pros only: season or career prize money in the competition's stated currency unit (whole units)
  match_win_pct              DERIVED: matches_won / (matches_won + matches_lost)
  games_win_pct              DERIVED: games_won / (games_won + games_lost)
  tiebreak_win_pct           DERIVED: tiebreaks_won / tiebreaks_played
Surface splits are scope split lines with split_label "Clay 2026", "Hard, career", "Indoor 2026", using the same keys.

PAIR LINES (STAT_OF the pair team): the same match, season and career keys as a player. Doubles rankings per pair use ranking and ranking_points on the pair's line; per-player doubles rankings use the same keys on the person's doubles season line, which is RECORDED_IN the doubles tour season (a separate competition) so singles and doubles rankings never share a line.

TEAM LINES (tie teams and league teams) are in Standings.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Tennis has three kinds of table and the pack keeps them apart.

1. Team competitions (national-team ties, college dual matches, club and association team leagues). Team season line, scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, rebuilt from the tie events' COMPETED_IN results and scores when its source is derived (an owner or official line is reported as it stands), keys:
  ties_played  ties_won  ties_lost  ties_drawn (where a league allows a drawn tie)
  rubbers_won  rubbers_lost
  sets_won  sets_lost
  games_won  games_lost
  points             league points when the competition uses them (scoring_system on the competition: win_loss, rubbers (one point per rubber won), 2-1-0, 3-1-0, custom)
  walkover_rubbers_received  walkover_rubbers_given
Columns to show: P W L (D) Rubbers for-against, Sets, Points when used. Default tiebreakers in order (override in House rules): points, ties won, head-to-head tie result, rubber difference, rubbers won, set difference, sets won, game difference, games won, then the competition's stated method (play-off or coin toss; say which).
Promotion and relegation between divisions are COMPETES_IN outcome promoted / relegated, group the division ("Division 2", "Men's 3.5 Flight A").

2. Tournament draws are brackets, not tables. Read the draw off the match events by stage; seeds and entry route are on COMPETES_IN to the season; the champion has outcome champion and final_rank 1, the runner-up final_rank 2 and outcome runner_up, semifinalists final_rank 3 (shared) and outcome eliminated with status eliminated. For a round-robin group inside a finals event, order the group by: matches won, then (two tied) head-to-head, then (three tied) sets won percentage, then games won percentage, then the competition's House rules. Say which rule split the tie.

3. Rankings and ratings are not standings tables: they are stored snapshots on person or pair season lines (ranking, ranking_points, rating, ladder_position). When asked for "the top 10" of a tour or club, read every entrant's season line for that season, order by ranking ascending (or rating descending, or ladder_position ascending), and state the as_of of the oldest line. Never compute a ranking from results: ranking systems have their own rolling windows and the pack does not reproduce them. A club ladder's order IS computed by the pack's ladder rules in the Recreational chunk, because ladders have no external authority.

Box leagues (round robin inside a box, one cycle per season): a person season line per entrant RECORDED_IN the cycle season with matches_played, matches_won, matches_lost, sets_won, sets_lost, games_won, games_lost, points (the box's own points scheme: commonly 3 for a win, 1 for a loss with a set won, 0 otherwise, or 1 per set won; House rules). Order the box by points, matches won, head-to-head, set difference, game difference. Top two outcome promoted, bottom two relegated, by default; House rules override.

Season result words: WON person or pair → season with title Champion, Runner-up; WON team → season with title Champion for a team competition; WON person → event with title for a within-match honour is rare and used only when the owner asks.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Singles has no roster. A person simply COMPETES_IN seasons and COMPETED_IN matches. Do not create a team for a singles player, ever.

Doubles pairs: a pair is a team with team_type pair. Both partners PLAYS_FOR it with started the first match together (or the day the owner names it), ended when they split, arrangement matching their level (contract for pros, amateur for club players), position deuce_side / ad_side when known. A pair has exactly two open PLAYS_FOR edges; a third person means a new pair. See Doubles pairs for naming and reuse.

Team competitions: the squad is PLAYS_FOR the national, school, club or recreational team as the base describes; position the usual lineup slot (S1..S6, D1..D3, singles, doubles, reserve). Before logging a tie lineup, check against the competition's House rules: how many singles and doubles rubbers; whether a player may play both a singles and a doubles rubber (college dual: yes; many club leagues: at most one singles and one doubles); lineup order rules (college: singles lineup in order of ability, a challenged "stacking" is noted in lore only if the owner says so); skill-level caps (association leagues: a team's level such as 3.5 is a tag on the team and a House rule, and a player's level is NOT stored on the person; the owner checks eligibility); gender rules for mixed and co-ed ties (not stored; the owner checks). Say in one line what you checked.

Availability for a tie: PLAYS_FOR.availability available / unavailable / doubtful / suspended, no reason, as the base says. A player who does not travel is simply not on the tie's PLAYED_IN edges.

Nominations and changes: a player nominated for a rubber and then replaced before it starts is PLAYED_IN the tie with played false and replaced_by the incoming player's slug; the incoming player's edge has played true. No reason is recorded.

Club membership is not a roster. A club with a ladder, box league and social play is a competition (or several) with level recreational and governing_body the club; its members are people who COMPETES_IN seasons. A club team entered in an inter-club league is a team with team_type club. Membership lists, fees and contact details are not stored on people (see the base privacy rule); the club secretary is STAFF_OF the competition with role other and title "Club secretary", the ladder organiser STAFF_OF with role commissioner.

Coaches: STAFF_OF person → the player's pair team, or, for a singles pro, a lore chunk on the person titled Coaching (STAFF_OF needs a team or competition target, and the pack does not create a team for a singles player). Team-tie captains who do not play are STAFF_OF the team with role head_coach and title "Captain"; a playing captain has PLAYS_FOR with role captain.

Minors: any U18 category competition marks its entrants is_minor true by default; first name and last initial, nothing else, per the base policy. Age-group categories live on the competition (tag u14, u18, over_35, over_60, wheelchair, adaptive) and are never used to infer a date of birth.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content:
OFFICIATED role values (record only when the owner names the person; most club and recreational matches have none, and players call their own lines):
  chair_umpire        the umpire in the chair; the base's "head" official for a match
  line_umpire         a line judge; one edge per named person
  referee             the tournament referee, responsible for the event; OFFICIATED the match only when they acted in it (a default, a weather decision), otherwise STAFF_OF the competition with role other and title "Referee"
  assistant_referee   deputy or assistant referee
  review_official     the official operating electronic review or line calling
  net_judge           where still used
  scorer              a club scorer or the person who kept the stats
  roving_umpire       a court-roving umpire covering several courts (club and junior events); OFFICIATED when they ruled on the match
  supervisor          the tour or association supervisor, when they ruled on the match
Electronic line calling with no human line umpires is a fact about the event, not an official: tag the event electronic-line-calling.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: (none yet: keys the owner adds go here, one per line, with the date and who asked)

lore.title: Doubles pairs
lore.content:
When to create a pair: the first time two people play a doubles match together that the owner wants recorded with a result. Search first: search_entities entity_type team, query both surnames; a pair that split and reunited is the same entity (set status active again and open new PLAYS_FOR edges, started the reunion date).

Name: "<Surname A> / <Surname B>" with the surnames in the order the competition prints them, otherwise alphabetical; use first names too when surnames clash inside the world ("Lee J. / Patel"). For the owner's own pair, tag it mine. short_name is the owner's phrase ("us", "the Tuesday pair"). team_type pair, status active, tags: tennis, pair, doubles (and mixed for a mixed pair).

Edges: each partner PLAYS_FOR the pair; the pair COMPETES_IN draws and leagues; the pair COMPETED_IN each doubles match; each partner PLAYED_IN each doubles match with for_team the pair slug (optional in rec play, useful when a pair's partner was substituted for one event); stat lines STAT_OF the pair (the pair's record, ranking, titles) and, when a box score splits serve stats by player, STAT_OF each person with for_team the pair slug.

Why a team and not a property: a pair has a record, a seed, a ranking, a title and a head-to-head of its own, which is everything the base means by a side. The alternative (two person edges with a partner property) would give the match four sides and the pair no record.

A one-night pair (social mixed, a pick-up partner): still a pair, status inactive after the event if they will not play again, or skip the result entirely and log the evening as an event with event_type other. Do not create a pair for a practice.

Partner-by-partner records ("my record with Sam vs with Lee") are read off the pairs the person PLAYS_FOR: one pair, one record. A person's overall doubles record is the sum of their pairs' records and is computed on request, not stored, unless the owner imports a published per-player doubles line (then a season line on the person, RECORDED_IN the doubles tour season).

lore.title: Tournaments and tours
lore.content:
The mapping, and why.

A recurring tournament (a major, a 1000-level or 500-level tour event, a national championship, the club championship) is a COMPETITION: format knockout (group_knockout for a round-robin-then-knockout finals event), level pro / international / college / youth / recreational, governing_body, region, match_format the default form of its matches (best_of_5 at the men's majors, best_of_3 almost everywhere else, best_of_3_match_tiebreak in most club play), tags tennis plus a tier tag (tier_major, tier_1000, tier_500, tier_250, tier_challenger, tier_futures, tier_national, tier_club) and a discipline tag (mens_singles, womens_singles, mens_doubles, womens_doubles, mixed_doubles, or open). Each discipline with its own draw is its own competition when the owner follows more than one ("Spring Major, women's singles" and "Spring Major, women's doubles"), because entrants, seeds and champions differ; a club championship with five draws is five small competitions or one competition with House rules saying the draws share a season, whichever the owner prefers (default: one competition per draw when seeds are tracked, one competition otherwise).

Each edition is a SEASON: label "2026", status, start_date/end_date, stage entries_open → qualifying → main_draw → completed, current_round the round in progress ("R16"), rounds_total the number of main-draw rounds (7 for a 128 draw). Tag the season with its own tag (spring_major_2026). When it belongs to a tour year, make it PART_OF the tour season (season to season) and also give it the tour-year tag (womens_tour_2026) so the year can be listed by tag. Entrants COMPETES_IN the season: seed (null for unseeded), entry (direct, qualifier, wild_card, lucky_loser, protected_ranking, alternate), group for round-robin groups, status entered → active → eliminated / withdrawn / completed, outcome champion / runner_up / eliminated / withdrew, final_rank 1, 2, 3 (shared), 5 (shared), 9, 17, 33, 65 for the round reached (the pack's convention: final_rank = 1 + the number of players who went further).

Matches are events PART_OF the season with stage the round code and round the human label, neutral_site true, sides neutral_first (printed higher in the draw) and neutral_second, HELD_AT the venue with field the court. A match that spans two days (rain, curfew) keeps its first date and gets end_date.

The TOUR YEAR (the men's tour, the women's tour, a national junior circuit, a regional seniors circuit, a club's annual calendar when it publishes a club ranking) is a COMPETITION with format league and scoring_system ranking_points, level pro or whichever fits, tag the tour. Its season "2026" is where the ranking stat lines live (person season line, RECORDED_IN the tour season, keys ranking, ranking_points, matches_won, matches_lost, titles, prize_money, as_of) and where the year-end finals event hangs if the owner does not make it its own competition. The tour season has no matches of its own; each tournament season that belongs to it is PART_OF the tour season and shares its tag. The pack once grouped tournament seasons by tag alone; PART_OF is now the structural link and the tag is a convenience.

Why tournaments are competitions and not parent events inside the tour season: seeds, entry route and the champion all need a season to hang on (COMPETES_IN and WON target seasons, not events); a tournament is a standing thing that runs year after year with a trophy, which is the base's definition of a competition; and the draw is then read off events by stage exactly as the base's seasons rule reads a playoff bracket. A one-off tournament inside a club's season (a weekend club event) may instead be a parent event with event_type match, stage final for the parent, and the matches PART_OF it; the sides' COMPETED_IN edges to the parent event carry that event's group, seed and final_rank. Use that only when nothing needs an entry route or a champion WON a season.

A tournament's doubles draw is a competition with discipline tag mens_doubles etc.; pairs COMPETES_IN its season; the two partners can also WON the season individually if the owner wants titles counted per person (title "Champion (doubles)"), but the pair is the side that COMPETED_IN the matches.

Team competitions with ties (a national-team competition, a college conference dual-match season, an inter-club league): the competition's format is league, league_playoffs, knockout or group_knockout as the competition runs; teams COMPETES_IN the season with group; each tie is a parent match event between the two teams (COMPETED_IN from each team, score the rubbers won, score_display "3-2"); each rubber is a child event PART_OF the tie with stage rubber, round the rubber label, and COMPETED_IN from the people or pairs who played it; squad members PLAYED_IN the tie with for_team and position the slot. Standings read the ties; rubber, set and game counts are on team season lines. A dead rubber not played: status cancelled, result no_result, lore "not played, tie decided"; a dead rubber shortened: decided_by shortened.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Retirement (a side stops mid-match): status completed, result to the opponent, decided_by retired, score_display the score at the stoppage plus " ret." (6-4 3-6 2-5 ret.), home_score/away_score the sets completed as they stood (the retiring side does not get credit for an unfinished set). The opponent's COMPETED_IN result win, the retiree's loss. matches_played counts it for both; retirements +1 on the retiree's season line. No reason is recorded anywhere, in any wording, as the base requires for retirements and walkovers.

Walkover (a side does not start): status forfeited, result to the opponent, decided_by walkover, score_display "w/o", home_score/away_score null and margin_type blank (not 2-0: no sets were played; standings use rubbers or matches, and this is the pack's awarded score for a forfeit: none). The opponent's walkovers_received +1, the withdrawing side's walkovers_given +1; neither side's matches_played changes. COMPETES_IN status withdrawn for the side that withdrew from the tournament. No reason is recorded. A lucky loser who takes the vacated draw spot gets COMPETES_IN entry lucky_loser and the walkover event is between the original two names only if the walkover happened after the draw was final; if the replacement happened before the first round, there is no walkover event at all, just the entry.

Default (the officials end the match or remove a side): status completed if points were played, forfeited if not; decided_by default; score_display with " def."; defaults +1 on the defaulted side's season line. No reason is recorded, in any wording.

Abandoned (weather, light, a venue problem, never resumed): status abandoned, result no_result, the score at the stoppage in score_display, decided_by blank. Rare in tennis: a suspended match resumes from the same score on a later day; it is one event, status suspended until it finishes, end_date the finishing day, then completed, with a lore chunk "Suspended at 4-4 in the second, resumed <date>". A match replayed from scratch (a club event whose rain-out is restarted) is a new event with round "Replay" naming the original in lore.

Postponed (never started, moved to a later date): status postponed, keep the event, update date_* when rescheduled, original date in lore, per the base.

Dead rubbers in a tie: not played: status cancelled, result no_result, lore "not played, tie decided", decided_by decided_tie on the TIE if its rubbers were cut short. Shortened: decided_by shortened, match_format on the rubber event set to the short form used.

Coin-toss or bye outcomes in club events: a bye is no event at all (the player simply appears in the next round); a club rule that decides an unplayable match by toss is decided_by coin_toss with House rules saying so.

Health, once more: ret., w/o, def. and withdrew are the whole fact. If the owner types "retired with cramp" store "ret." and say, once, that the reason stays out of this world.

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What changes at club and recreational level.

Formats: best_of_3_match_tiebreak is the default; pro sets and timed sessions are common; no-ad scoring is a House rule. Put the club's default in match_format on each competition.

Officials: none. Players call their own lines; a disputed call is lore if the owner wants it. A club tournament may have a referee (STAFF_OF the competition) and roving umpires.

Box leagues: one competition per box league (format round_robin, level recreational, scoring_system custom with the points scheme in House rules). Each cycle (month, six weeks, quarter) is a season labelled by the cycle ("March 2026", "Cycle 3 2026"); boxes are COMPETES_IN.group ("Box 3"); every match in the box is an event PART_OF the cycle season with stage regular_season (or box); each entrant has a season line with the box keys (Standings 3). At the cycle's end set outcome promoted / relegated / none and open the next cycle with the boxes re-drawn; the base's season-rollover routine applies, with groups moved rather than carried. Unplayed box matches at cycle end: status cancelled, result no_result; House rules say whether an unplayed match is scored as a double loss or a walkover to the player who tried to arrange it (then decided_by walkover with w/o).

Ladders: one competition with format ladder, level recreational, scoring_system custom. One season per year (or per the club's reset). Entrants COMPETES_IN the season; the current position is ladder_position on the entrant's season line (as_of the last change), not on the edge, because it changes with every challenge. A challenge is an event with stage ladder, round "Challenge", the challenger first-named (neutral_first), score_display the result, home_score/away_score sets or games per match_format. Default ladder rule (override in House rules): a challenger may challenge up to N places above (default 3); if the challenger wins, the challenger takes the loser's position and everyone between moves down one; if the challenger loses, nothing moves; a challenge not accepted within the club's window is a walkover to the challenger. After logging a challenge, update ladder_position on every affected entrant's line and list the moves in a lore chunk on the event titled Ladder moves. When asked for the ladder, read every entrant's season line, order by ladder_position, state the oldest as_of.

Club championships: a competition per draw (or one with House rules), format knockout, a season per year; the pattern is the tournament pattern with entry mostly direct and seeds often absent (null).

Association and club team leagues (a team of 3.5-level players in a national association's adult league, a county inter-club league): the tie-and-rubber pattern. The team's level is a tag on the team (level_3_5) and a House rule; a player's rating is on their own season or career line (rating) only if the owner wants it, and is never used by the AI to judge eligibility. Flights, divisions and areas are COMPETES_IN.group ("Flight A", "Area 2"). Playoffs beyond the local league (sectionals, nationals) are further seasons of the same competition or a parent competition; one competition per level is simplest.

Social and sporadic play: a hit the owner wants remembered is an event with stage friendly; a practice set is event_type practice with no result. Partners rotate; pairs for social play are optional (see Doubles pairs).

Sporadic stats: most club players keep the score and nothing else. Match lines are optional; the AI never asks for serve stats unless the owner has given them once. When a season line is derived from a partial set of match lines, say how many matches it covers, as the base requires.

Ratings: a club or association rating (a skill level such as 3.5, or a dynamic rating system's number) is rating on the person's season line (if the system is yearly) or career line (if rolling). The system's name goes in House rules on the competition that uses it; the AI never computes a rating.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level adds.

Tiers and tours: the men's tour, the women's tour, their second-tier circuits, the four majors run by their own federations, the national-team competitions, the year-end finals, team exhibition events. Each tournament is a competition with a tier tag; each tour year is a competition with format league and scoring_system ranking_points (Tournaments and tours). A player's season line on the tour season carries ranking, ranking_points, matches_won, matches_lost, titles, prize_money.

Draw mechanics the pack records: seeds (COMPETES_IN.seed, 32 seeds in a 128 draw, 16 in 64, 8 in 32), entry routes (direct, qualifier, wild_card, lucky_loser, protected_ranking, alternate), byes for top seeds (no event), retirements and walkovers (Forfeits chunk), a final_rank per round reached.

Formats: best_of_5 with a 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 in the fifth at the men's majors (match_format best_of_5_match_tiebreak); best_of_3 elsewhere; doubles on tour best_of_3_match_tiebreak with no-ad as a House rule; mixed doubles often shortened formats. Electronic line calling is a tag on the event; the chair umpire is OFFICIATED chair_umpire.

Modern stats: the full Stat keys list, including serve speeds (km/h), rally length, distance covered, net points, forehand/backhand splits, dominance ratio (derived). Imported box scores set source import and source_url; percentages given without components are STORED-IF-GIVEN with components null.

Rankings: stored snapshots only. Never derive a ranking from results; ranking systems have rolling 52-week windows, countable-event caps and bonus rules the pack does not reproduce. Record what the owner or the import says, with as_of. ranking_high on the career line.

Prize money: prize_money on season and career lines, in whole units of the currency named in House rules on the tour competition (default: the tour's published currency). Not stored for private people.

Coaching changes and sponsorships: a coaching change is an event with event_type other and INVOLVED_IN role subject (player) and subject (coach) with detail "joined as coach" / "left"; the coach is STAFF_OF the player's pair team if one exists, otherwise a lore chunk Coaching on the player (the base has no person → person staff edge). Sponsorship is not tracked.

Team tennis at the top level (national-team competitions, team exhibition leagues): the tie-and-rubber pattern; national teams are team_type national with the squad PLAYS_FOR and a non-playing captain STAFF_OF role head_coach title "Captain". Ties over two or three days carry end_date. Finals weeks with group stages: stage group_stage on the ties, COMPETES_IN.group on the teams.

Suspensions and bans: PLAYS_FOR.availability suspended where a team edge exists; for a singles pro the ban's sporting terms (dates, events missed) go in a lore chunk on the person as the base allows for disciplinary matters; anti-doping matters are recorded only as the governing body's published sporting sanction (dates), never with any medical or substance detail.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content: Fantasy tennis is uncommon and the pack ships no slots, scoring table or roster defaults. Bracket-challenge games (pick the winner of every match in a draw) are the closest common thing: if the owner runs one, treat each participant's bracket as a team with team_type fantasy in a competition with level fantasy and format league, one season per tournament edition, and score each participant's season line with picks_correct, picks_total, bracket_points (the pool's own scheme, House rules). Weekly head-to-head fantasy matchups with player match lines carrying fantasy_points, if a platform offers them, follow the base's rule/app_fantasy with these sport-specific keys only: fantasy_points, projected_points on the real player's match line; a default scoring table is deliberately not supplied. Add to Extended keys if a pool needs more.

lore.title: Other racket sports
lore.content:
This chunk tells the next five packs what to copy and what to change. Each gets its own pack (code pickleball, padel, badminton, table_tennis, squash) with its own Stat keys; the structural pattern is this one.

Copy unchanged: a person is a side (COMPETED_IN, COMPETES_IN from person; no PLAYED_IN edge in singles); a doubles pair is a team with team_type pair; tournaments are competitions with editions as seasons, each tournament season PART_OF the tour or circuit season, the tour or circuit year a competition with format league and scoring_system ranking_points; COMPETES_IN carries seed, entry and final_rank; match_format on the competition with an event override; the game-by-game or set-by-set line in the event's periods array with score_display the human line; per-game or per-set stats as scope segment lines; margin_type games (or sets where sets are played); team ties are parent events with rubbers as children; rankings and ratings are stored snapshots on season or career lines; retirements, walkovers and defaults carry no reason; box leagues and ladders as in Recreational; officials only when named.

Change per sport (the single score number and match_format vocabulary):
  Pickleball: the score number is GAMES WON (2-1 in best of three to 11); score_display the points per game "11-7 9-11 11-4". Scoring system is a competition property: scoring_system side_out (only the serving side scores, games to 11 win by 2, score called as three numbers server-receiver-server number) or rally (every rally scores, commonly to 15 or 21, with the freeze rule as a House rule). match_format values: best_of_3_to_11, game_to_11, game_to_15, game_to_21, best_of_3_to_15, timed. Stat keys add: serves_won, side_outs, third_shot_drops, dinks_won, kitchen_faults (non-volley-zone faults), ernes, atps (around-the-post winners). Ratings: a dynamic rating system's number (e.g. a 2.0-8.0 scale) is rating on the career line, with the system named in House rules; a self-rated skill level is a tag on the entrant for the season (rating_3_5), not on the person.
  Padel: always doubles; pairs are the only sides in competition. Scoring as tennis (sets of games, golden point as a House rule); score number sets won. Stat keys add: smashes_won, bandeja_winners, vibora_winners, wall_errors, lob_winners. Rankings per player on the circuit season line, per pair on the pair's line.
  Badminton: score number GAMES WON (best of three to 21, rally scoring, win by 2, cap at 30); score_display "21-15 18-21 21-19". match_format best_of_3_to_21, best_of_5_to_11 (variant), single_game_to_21. Stat keys add: smash_winners, net_kills, drop_winners, clears, service_faults, longest_rally_shots. Disciplines as tags: mens_singles, womens_singles, mens_doubles, womens_doubles, mixed_doubles. Team ties with five rubbers follow the tie pattern.
  Table tennis: score number GAMES WON (best of five or seven to 11, win by 2); score_display "11-7 9-11 11-4 11-9". match_format best_of_5_to_11, best_of_7_to_11, best_of_3_to_11. Stat keys add: service_points_won, receive_points_won, forehand_loops_won, backhand_winners, edge_balls, timeouts_used. Team events: ties with singles rubbers and one doubles, often with a tie decided at 3.
  Squash: score number GAMES WON (best of five to 11, point-a-rally, win by 2); score_display "11-6 8-11 11-9 11-7". match_format best_of_5_to_11, best_of_3_to_11, best_of_5_to_9_hand_in_hand_out (traditional). Stat keys add: strokes_awarded, lets_called, no_lets, winners, unforced_errors, rally_length_avg. Team ties of three or five rubbers; the referee and marker are OFFICIATED roles referee and marker.

In every one of these, a retirement, walkover or default is recorded exactly as the tennis Forfeits chunk says, with no reason; the set-by-set stat line keys that stay the same (games_won, games_lost, sets_won, sets_lost, matches_played, matches_won, matches_lost, walkovers_received, walkovers_given, retirements, defaults, titles, ranking, ranking_points, rating, ladder_position) are copied as they are.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: ace: serve untouched by the returner. ad / advantage: the point after deuce. ad side: the left service court. all: level score ("30-all"). alternate: a player who enters when a spot opens. back draw / consolation: the losers' draw. bagel: a 6-0 set (slang). box league: a small round-robin group that promotes and relegates each cycle. break: winning a game on the opponent's serve. break point: a point that would win the receiver the game. bye: advancing a round without a match. challenge: an electronic review request, or a ladder match request. chair umpire: the match official. dead rubber: a rubber in a tie whose result cannot change the tie. deuce: 40-40. deuce side: the right service court. default (def.): a side removed from the match by the officials. direct acceptance: entry by ranking. double fault: two consecutive faults, point lost. draw: the bracket. dual match: a college team match of singles and doubles rubbers. golden point / no-ad: deciding point at deuce. hold: winning your own service game. ladder: a challenge-based club ranking. love: zero. lucky loser: a qualifying loser who gets a vacated main-draw spot. main draw: the tournament proper after qualifying. match tiebreak: a 10-point tiebreak in place of a deciding set. mixed: a man and a woman as a pair. no-ad: no advantage scoring. pro set: a set to 8 (or 10) games. protected ranking: entry on a ranking frozen after a long absence; the absence itself is never explained in this world. qualifier (Q): a player who came through qualifying. rally: the exchange of shots. retired (ret.): a side stopped mid-match. rubber: one match inside a team tie. seed: a ranked entrant placed in the draw so seeds meet late. set: six games (two clear) or a tiebreak. tie: a team match of several rubbers; in this world never a drawn result. tiebreak: the game that decides a set at 6-6. walkover (w/o): a match not started because one side withdrew. wild card (WC): an entry granted by the organiser. winner: a shot the opponent cannot touch.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Tour year (pro): the tour season runs January to November; hard-court swing to open the year, a clay swing in spring ending at the clay major, a short grass swing ending at the grass major, a North American hard-court swing ending at the late-summer major, indoor and Asian hard courts in autumn, the year-end finals in November, national-team finals late in the year, then an offseason of roughly five weeks. Rankings update weekly on Mondays; the as_of on ranking lines is a Monday. Make each tournament season PART_OF the tour season and tag it with the tour-year tag so the AI can list the year either way.

Majors: each is a competition with a two-week season; mens and womens singles, mens, womens and mixed doubles, wheelchair and junior draws are separate competitions in the same fortnight sharing a tag (spring_major_2026).

College (dual matches): autumn individual tournaments, then a January to May dual-match season with a conference championship and a national team championship in May; the individual national championships follow.

Club: a year-long club season with the ladder open all year, box leagues in monthly or six-week cycles, the club championships in late summer, inter-club league seasons in spring and summer (and winter indoor where courts exist). Each is its own competition; the club's year is a tag.

Association adult leagues: local league spring to summer, then sectional and national playoffs for winners in autumn. One competition per level and age division, seasons per year.

Juniors: age-group calendars by national federation; one competition per event and age group, is_minor handling per the base policy.

Offseason work: season rollover per the base (new tour season, new club cycles), ranking lines carried as new season lines with the year-end numbers as the first snapshot.

properties.trigger: a tennis match, ladder challenge, box-league match, rubber or tournament round just happened or is being followed; logging a tennis score or match stats; a tennis record, head-to-head, surface record, ranking, ladder, box table or draw question
properties.scope: event, stat_line, person, team, season, competition

data.short_description: The post-match log for tennis, in order: find the season, the sides (person or pair), the event; score it with sets (or games) as the number and the full line in score_display; retirements and walkovers with no reason; optional match stats; ripple to the draw, ladder, box or tie; then the story. Also how to answer record, head-to-head, surface, ranking, ladder and draw questions honestly.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The owner just played, or is following a tournament, and wants a tennis result on the books: a singles or doubles match, a ladder challenge, a box-league match, a rubber in a team tie, or a round of a tournament. Also how to answer "what's my record", "head-to-head", "the ladder" and "the draw" honestly. Read rule/sport_tennis first for vocabulary.

lore.title: Logging a match
lore.content:
1. Find the context. Which competition and season: the owner's club ladder, the March box, the spring major's women's singles 2026, this weekend's league tie. search_entities entity_type season with the competition name; if the owner names a tournament with no competition yet, create it per Tournaments and tours (confirm the tier and discipline in one question).
2. Find or create the sides. Singles: the person (search by name; create with primary_role player and the tennis tag if new; is_minor if the competition is a junior age group). Doubles: the pair (search both surnames; create per Doubles pairs). A tie: both teams, then the rubbers' sides.
3. Find the event. A scheduled event often exists (the draw or fixture list was loaded); update it rather than creating. Otherwise create: event_type match, name "<First> vs <Second> — <date>" (add the round when it matters: "— R16"), PART_OF the season (or the tie), stage and round, match_format if it differs from the competition's default, neutral_site true unless a club tie has a host, HELD_AT the venue with field the court if known, tags tennis, match, the season tag.
4. Score it, before anything else. Read match_format to know what the score number is (sets in best-of formats, games in pro sets and timed play, rubbers on a tie). score_display the full line as tennis writes it; periods per set when the owner wants the line queryable; margin_type sets or games with margin. status completed, result, decided_by (regulation, retired, walkover, default), COMPETED_IN from each side with side and result. For a retirement or walkover follow Forfeits and abandonments exactly and store no reason.
5. Ask one question only if needed: "Want the match stats, or just the score?" Most club owners want the score. If stats: one stat_line per side (STAT_OF the person or pair, RECORDED_IN the match, scope match, keys from Stat keys, nulls for anything not counted, completeness, source owner); per-set splits as scope segment lines. Store counts, not percentages, when both are given; store the percentage with null components when only the percentage is known.
6. Ripple. Tournament: the loser's COMPETES_IN status eliminated, final_rank per round; the winner's next scheduled match gets its second COMPETED_IN edge if the opponent is now known. Ladder: apply the ladder rule, update ladder_position on every affected season line, lore chunk Ladder moves on the event. Box: update the entrant's season line (matches, sets, games, points). Tie: update the tie's score and score_display, and when the tie is decided, its result and the teams' season lines. Season lines derived from match lines: update in the same breath, source derived, as_of the match date.
7. The story goes in lore on the event (Summary, Key moments, Conditions) in the owner's words. Match duration, if given and the owner does not want it as a stat, goes here.

lore.title: Answering questions
lore.content:
Record: walk the person's (or pair's) COMPETED_IN edges for the season, count win/loss; walkovers received are not wins played, so say "12-4 in matches played, plus two walkovers" when they exist. Say the season and how many matches.
Head-to-head: match events with a COMPETED_IN edge from each side, in date order, from the first-named person's point of view; name the most recent meeting and the surface if HELD_AT venues carry it.
Surface record: group the person's completed matches by the venue's surface; say how many matches had no venue on file.
Ranking: read the person's season line on the tour season; give ranking and ranking_points with as_of. Never compute a ranking from results. If the owner asks "how many points does she need", say the pack does not model the ranking system.
Ladder or box table: read every entrant's season line, order by ladder_position (or the box points scheme), state the oldest as_of; rebuild box lines from COMPETED_IN edges when any line is older than the latest match.
The draw: read the season's events by stage, show the bracket round by round; a scheduled match with one side is "v. winner of ...".
Serve stats: derive percentages from stored counts and say how many matches the counts cover; when a stored percentage has null components, say it was given, not computed.

lore.title: Things not to do
lore.content: Do not create a team for a singles player. Do not record why anyone retired, withdrew or gave a walkover. Do not store a skill level, age group or disability class on a person; they belong to the competition. Do not infer age from a junior or seniors category. Do not look up a club player, a junior or a rating-system profile on the web. Do not copy the score into a stat line (games_won on a match line is a stat the owner asked for, not a copy of the score; include it only when the owner wants per-match game counts summed into a season line).
